accounting.rationale: J3/24-007 PDF 75, printed 61, line 22: three aspects of a typed value's denotation. Their actual syntax and semantics retain the canonical owners rather than acquiring duplicate local S IDs.

The denotation identifies the type of the value. R604/R605 and the literal/constructor definitions are dependencies, not new requirements owned here. BOZ remains typeless under 7.7 p1 (PDF 113), despite being an R605 literal alternative.

The denotation identifies applicable type parameters. Kind suffixes use supported source-level kind values, not universal 1/4/8 byte codes; character length, kind, array shape and derived-type parameters remain distinct. Enum and enumeration types have no parameters (7.6.1-.2).

The denotation identifies a particular value within its type/parameter domain. Processor-dependent real approximation and character repertoires remain qualified; the phrase does not prescribe IEEE arithmetic or native ASCII.

PDF 75 line 23 delegates intrinsic literal syntax to 7.4. The existing 6.2.3 constants catalogue accounts for literal/named alternatives and leaves individual spellings with their canonical rules; no unrelated negative is duplicated.
PDF 75 lines 24-28: each of four constructors denotes a constant value only with the stated constant-expression premise.

A structure constructor meeting 10.1.12 denotes a scalar derived constant. 7.5.10 (PDF 106-109) and 10.1.12 p1(3) (PDF 187) preserve component accessibility, permitted initialization targets and NULL for allocatable components. An arbitrary function call or constructor with runtime components is not made constant.

A constant-expression enum constructor denotes a scalar enum constant. 7.6.1/R765/C7113/p7 (PDF 110) requires an integer or BOZ operand and a representable value; 10.1.12 p1(4) supplies constancy. Integer enumerators are not themselves enum-typed constants.

A constant-expression enumeration constructor denotes a scalar enumeration constant. 7.6.2/R771/p5 (PDF 112) restricts the integer ordinal to the enumerators' range; 10.1.12 p1(5) adds constancy. No out-of-range result is evaluated.

An array constructor meeting 10.1.12 denotes a constant array of intrinsic or nonintrinsic type. 7.8 (PDF 114-115) separately supplies rank one, same-type/kind premises, length agreement without a type-spec, and conversion with a type-spec. 10.1.12 p1(2) and its closing condition (PDF 187-188) require constant elements, implied-DO controls and parameter/subscript expressions. Rank is not another type or kind.

PDF 75 line 29 permits naming a constant value; it does not require every constant to be named. 8.5.13 (PDF 130-131) and 8.6.11 (PDF 139) define PARAMETER, prior definition, conversion and shape restrictions. Existing R606/R607 constant-name controls retain ownership. This source-accounting permission is not an implementation pass.
